open_points.subject: A1 — file identity after directory listing
open_points.text: A name is judged as the directory listing returns it, and that judgement holds for the whole scan. A file renamed after the listing is no longer at the listed path, so reading it for placing fails with `unreadable_file` (A3 rule 4).
open_points.question: If the listed file is renamed but another regular file appears at the same listed path before it is opened, must placement reject the identity change with `unreadable_file`, process the replacement using the original name judgement, or reclassify the replacement?
options: Remember the listed file's identity and reject any replacement with `unreadable_file`.
Open the listed path and process whichever regular file is there, retaining the original name judgement.
Re-list or reclassify the replacement as a newly observed file.
open_points.default_guess: Remember the listed file's identity and reject a different object at that path with `unreadable_file`.

witness.initial: The scan lists an ordinary regular file `a.jpg`.
events: Another actor renames the listed file to `b.jpg`.
The actor creates a different valid regular file at `a.jpg`.
The deliverer reaches the listed `a.jpg` and opens it for placement.
outcomes: The deliverer detects that the listed object was replaced and returns `unreadable_file` without writing.
The deliverer reads and places the new file found at `a.jpg` under the judgement made for the original directory entry.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees either a refusal or a successful placement of different content.

open_points.subject: A1 INV-18 — placing a conflict copy by hash
open_points.text: a conflict copy in the folder and in a subfolder, each with the mark in lower, upper and mixed case, is absent from the scan and placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent` and writes nothing (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`). Only the letters A to Z are folded (`test_only_ascii_letters_fold_in_the_conflict_mark`). Placed content replays when only a conflict copy still holds it (`test_placed_content_replays_when_only_a_conflict_copy_still_holds_it`)
open_points.question: Is the required failure when placing a conflict copy by hash limited to content that has no existing placement, while already placed content must replay?
options: The failure case starts with no existing placement; an existing placement replays.
The conflict-copy failure takes precedence even when a placement already exists.
The placement operation must distinguish how the hash was obtained.
open_points.default_guess: Limit the failure test to content with no existing placement and replay an existing placement.

witness.initial: Only a conflict copy containing source hash H remains in the folder, and a placement for project P and H already exists.
events: The caller asks to place H for project P.
outcomes: The placed-content clause replays the existing placement.
witness.observer: The caller sees either an error or the existing placement.

open_points.subject: A1 INV-18 — ordinary file disappears before placement
open_points.text: Placed content replays when only a conflict copy still holds it (`test_placed_content_replays_when_only_a_conflict_copy_still_holds_it`), an ordinary file with the content of a conflict copy is placed (`test_an_ordinary_file_is_placed_when_a_conflict_copy_has_the_same_content`). When that ordinary file disappears before it is read for placing, the conflict copy is not read in its place: the photo fails with `unreadable_file` and nothing is written (`test_a_conflict_copy_is_never_read_in_place_of_the_ordinary_file`).
open_points.question: Must the disappearing-ordinary-file failure test start without an existing placement, or does `unreadable_file` override replay when that content was already placed?
options: The failure scenario has no existing placement; placed content still replays.
Disappearance of the selected ordinary file produces `unreadable_file` even when the content already has a placement.
open_points.default_guess: State that the failure scenario has no existing placement; otherwise replay the existing placement.

witness.initial: An ordinary file and a conflict copy contain hash H, and a placement for project P and H already exists.
events: A scan observes the ordinary file.
The ordinary file disappears before the placement request reads it.
The caller requests placement of H for project P.
outcomes: The replay rule returns the existing placement without reading the conflict copy.
The disappearing-file rule returns `unreadable_file` without writing.
witness.observer: The caller sees either a replayed placement or an error.

open_points.subject: A1 — renamed file refusal
open_points.text:
A file renamed after the listing is no longer at the listed path, so reading it for placing fails
with `unreadable_file` (A3 rule 4).
open_points.rule:
Член, названный одним значением, — нарушение: значение с точкой или дефисом не является именем ни одного члена, генератор пишет только имена
(`AuditAction.EXPENSE_CREATE`), и валидатор отклоняет такую note
(`note_enum_member_by_value`).
open_points.question: Name the member by its generated member name beside the address of its model enumeration, with `unreadable_file` only as an optional value.

open_points.subject: A1 INV-18 — required refusal results
open_points.text: When that ordinary file disappears before it is read for placing, the conflict copy is not read in its place: the photo fails with `unreadable_file` and nothing is written (`test_a_conflict_copy_is_never_read_in_place_of_the_ordinary_file`). And a file renamed to a conflict copy after the listing fails with `unreadable_file` and writes nothing (`test_a_file_renamed_to_a_conflict_copy_after_the_scan_is_not_placed`).
open_points.rule:
Член, названный одним значением, — нарушение: значение с точкой или дефисом не является именем ни одного члена, генератор пишет только имена
(`AuditAction.EXPENSE_CREATE`), и валидатор отклоняет такую note
(`note_enum_member_by_value`).
open_points.question: Replace each value-only `unreadable_file` reference with the generated member name beside the address of its model enumeration.
